mainTopic: Trusting an עם הארץ on purity: inheritance, a check made for the פסח, flasks, and potters near מודיעים
overview: The amud opens with a משנה about a חבר and an עם הארץ who inherit from their father. They may split same-kind items by location, but they may not swap different kinds, and a ברייתא adds that the חבר burns wet produce and keeps dry. The גמרא then discusses whether a check of a בית הפרס made for the קרבן פסח also allows eating תרומה. עולא says yes and רבה בר עולא says no, and an old man supports עולא from our משנה about a רביעית of קודש. Next, a ברייתא says an עם הארץ is not believed about flasks, and the גמרא explains which flasks it means. It also reads the משנה's 'mixed jugs' as טבל kept pure for נסכים. אביי learns from the 'seventy days before the winepress' that a tenant farmer must prepare flasks then. A new משנה rules that potters inside מודיעים are believed about clay vessels, and a ברייתא explains when מודיעים itself counts as inside or outside. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Dividing wheat by location
steps.stepSummary: A חבר and an עם הארץ who inherit from their עם הארץ father may split the wheat by location.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a חבר and an עם הארץ inherit from their father, who was an עם הארץ, the חבר may say to his brother: 'You take the wheat in that place, and I'll take the wheat in this place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה about two brothers dividing an inheritance. The חבר is allowed to choose which pile of wheat he takes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חבר knows which pile of wheat stayed pure and wants that one. Since both piles are wheat, each brother is simply receiving his own share of the inheritance. Through ברירה, the pile each brother ends up with counts as his from the start, so this is not a trade with the עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who has committed to be careful about laws of purity (טהרה) and tithes
A person who is not careful about laws of purity and tithes

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the חבר selling or trading to his brother. Both piles are the same kind, so each brother is just taking his own share.

phrases.english: A חבר and an עם הארץ
who inherited from their father, who was an עם הארץ,
the חבר can say to him:
You take the wheat that is in such-and-such a place,
and I will take the wheat that is in such-and-such a place.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָבֵר וְעַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁיָּרְשׁוּ אֶת אֲבִיהֶם עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the quoted source
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חבר may divide same-type inherited items by location with his עם הארץ brother.

steps.title: Dividing wine by location
steps.stepSummary: The same rule applies to wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may also say: 'You take the wine in that place, and I'll take the wine in this place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of the same rule, this time with wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new about the logic is added. The wine example shows that the rule works for any item, as long as both shares are the same kind.

phrases.english: You take the wine that is in such-and-such a place,
and I will take the wine that is in such-and-such a place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same rule to a second item
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine may also be divided by location.

steps.title: No swapping between different kinds
steps.stepSummary: The חבר may not offer wet for dry or wheat for barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he may not say: 'You take the wet produce and I'll take the dry,' or 'You take the wheat and I'll take the barley.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets a limit on the rule. The חבר cannot split the inheritance by giving different kinds of items to each brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the two shares are different kinds, ברירה does not apply, so the division counts as a trade. That would mean the חבר is handing produce that can become טמא to an עם הארץ, which he is not allowed to do.

keyTerms.meaning: Wet produce, which can become טמא
Dry produce, which has not been made able to become טמא

steps.whatToRemember: Same kind of item means sharing an inheritance, which is allowed. Different kinds means a trade, which is not allowed.

phrases.english: But he may not say to him:
You take the wet produce and I will take the dry,
phrases.notes: Produce that got wet can become טמא. Dry produce cannot.

phrases.english: You take the wheat and I will take the barley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from steps 1 and 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dividing by different kinds counts as a trade and is forbidden.

steps.title: The חבר burns the wet and keeps the dry
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on this משנה says the חבר burns the wet produce he receives but keeps the dry produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא taught on this משנה: That חבר burns the wet produce and leaves the dry produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא that comments on the משנה. It tells us what the חבר does with the produce that ends up in his share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet produce from an עם הארץ is assumed to have become טמא, so the חבר burns it, which is what is done with טמא תרומה. Dry produce was never able to become טמא, so he may keep it. This teaches that the עם הארץ's dry produce is not considered טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught about it: introduces a ברייתא commenting on a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: An עם הארץ's wet produce is treated as טמא, but his dry produce is treated as pure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא shows how far we suspect an עם הארץ's produce of being טמא: only wet produce, not dry.

phrases.english: And it was taught about it:
that חבר burns the wet produce,
and leaves the dry produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A ברייתא adds to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חבר burns the inherited wet produce and keeps the dry.

steps.title: Why not keep the wet produce until the next winepress season?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חבר must burn the wet תרומה. Couldn't he simply keep it until the next גת season, when an עם הארץ's purity is trusted?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why must he burn it? Let him leave it until the next winepress season!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא from step 4: why burn the wet תרומה when it could be saved for the next winepress season? Because the ברייתא does not offer that option, the גמרא wants to learn from it that one may not hold the תרומה over like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the season of the גת, even an עם הארץ is careful about טהרה and is trusted. So holding the תרומה until then looks like an easy way to avoid burning it. Since the ברייתא says to burn it, it seems such holding over is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him leave it aside / hold it over
Winepress; here the winepress season, when even an עם הארץ is trusted about purity

phrases.english: Why? (Why must he burn the wet produce?)
Let him leave it for the coming winepress season!
phrases.notes: At winepress time even an עם הארץ is careful about purity, so his תרומה would count as pure then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about step 4's rule that the wet produce is burned, and tries to learn from it that one may not hold it over to the next winepress season.
steps.raayaObject: That one may not hold an עם הארץ's תרומה over until the next winepress season.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in step 4, which says to burn the wet produce and does not mention holding it over.

steps.title: The case is about something with no winepress
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a liquid that has no winepress season at all, so there is no future time when it would become trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to something that has no winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. The ברייתא is about a liquid that is never made in a winepress, so waiting would not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trust at winepress time only covers liquids made in a winepress. For any other liquid, no such season ever comes, so burning is the only option. That means the ברייתא proves nothing about whether one may hold produce over.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that has no winepress season

phrases.english: With something that has no winepress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5's proof by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא that holding over is not allowed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For this kind of liquid there is no winepress season to wait for, so the ברייתא says nothing about holding over.

steps.title: Then let him keep it until the רגל
steps.stepSummary: Even without a winepress season, he could keep the produce until the next רגל, when everyone is trusted about purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him leave it until the Festival!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Even something with no winepress could be kept until the next רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the שלש רגלים, even an עם הארץ is trusted on טהרה. So there is still a time when the תרומה would count as pure, and burning still seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Pilgrimage Festival (פסח, שבועות, סוכות), when even an עם הארץ is trusted about purity

phrases.english: Then let him leave it for the Festival!
phrases.notes: On the רגל, everyone is treated as pure, so this תרומה would count as pure then too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 6's answer by offering another time he could wait for.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 6 that the produce has no winepress season.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רגל also makes an עם הארץ trusted, so he could wait for it instead of burning.

steps.title: It would spoil before the רגל
steps.stepSummary: The case is about something that would not last until the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to something that will not keep until the Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the produce would go bad before the רגל arrives, so waiting is not a real option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is no winepress season and it cannot last until the רגל, burning is the only choice. So the ברייתא still teaches nothing about whether holding over is allowed, and that question stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא cannot prove that holding an עם הארץ's תרומה over is forbidden. It is about produce with no winepress season that would also spoil before the רגל.

phrases.english: With something that does not keep until the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could hold the produce until the רגל instead of burning it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce would spoil first, so burning is required, and no proof can be drawn.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: he is believed about a רביעית of קודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if the giver says he put a רביעית of sacred wine or oil into the barrel, he is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he said: I separated into it a quarter-log of sacred material, he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. It quotes it here to set up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עם הארץ is normally not trusted on טהרה for תרומה. But when he says the barrel holds a רביעית of קודש, he is believed, because people treat קודש with extra care. The next steps bring a related משנה to help understand this.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, a set liquid measure
Sacred, meaning consecrated items for the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And if he said: I separated into it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the barrel of תרומה wine or oil he is handing over.

phrases.english: a quarter-log of sacred material, he is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר הִפְרַשְׁתִּי לְתוֹכָהּ רְבִיעִית קֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עם הארץ who says he put a רביעית of קודש into the barrel is believed.

steps.title: A משנה elsewhere: checking for the פסח but not for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in אהלות. בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that we check for those bringing the קרבן פסח, but not for those eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that we check for those bringing the פסח, and we do not check for those eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה that also gives special treatment to holy matters. It is setting up a question about what 'checking' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both schools agree there is a leniency, a 'check', for people on their way to bring the פסח. The same leniency is not given for eating תרומה. What this check actually is gets explained next.

phrases.english: We learned there:
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
that we check for those bringing the Pesach offering,
and we do not check for those eating teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: מוֹדִין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related source to the topic of step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We check for those bringing the פסח but not for those eating תרומה.

steps.title: What does 'checking' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of check the משנה in אהלות means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'we check'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word בודקין means in that משנה. The answers come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never says what is being checked or how. The גמרא needs to define the term before it can understand the rule.

phrases.english: What is 'we check'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of checking the משנה means.

steps.title: שמואל: blowing on the בית הפרס while walking
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that a person blows on the ground of a בית הפרס as he walks through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A person blows on a בית הפרס as he goes.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that 'checking' means blowing on the ground of a בית הפרס while walking through it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הפרס is a field where a grave was plowed up, so small pieces of bone may be scattered there. Blowing moves any small bones out of the way, so the person stays pure. This is enough for the פסח but not for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed over, so it may hold small bone pieces

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A person blows on a beit haperas and keeps walking.
phrases.notes: The blowing clears away any tiny bone pieces in his path, so he stays pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מְנַפֵּחַ אָדָם בֵּית הַפְּרָס וְהוֹלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Checking means blowing on the ground of a בית הפרס while walking through it.

steps.title: עולא: a trodden בית הפרס is pure for the פסח
steps.stepSummary: עולא says a בית הפרס that has been trodden down is pure for those bringing the פסח. The reason is that the רבנן did not keep their rule in force where כרת is at stake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of עולא: A בית הפרס that was trodden down is pure for those bringing the פסח. They did not keep their words in force where כרת is involved.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a different explanation of 'checking': you check whether the field has been trodden down by people walking through it. He also explains why the רבנן were lenient here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of a בית הפרס is only a rule of the רבנן. Missing the קרבן פסח is punished with כרת, so they did not let their rule stop someone from bringing it. For תרומה there is no כרת at stake, so the leniency does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: That has been trodden down by passersby
They did not keep their decree in force
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for not bringing the פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a broad rule: a decree of the רבנן can step aside when keeping it would stop someone from a מצוה that carries כרת.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views of 'checking': שמואל says blowing on the ground, and עולא says checking whether the field was trodden down. The leniency is for the פסח only, because the רבנן did not keep their rule in force where כרת is at stake.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said in the name of Ulla:
A beit haperas that has been trodden down
phrases.notes: People walking through have packed down a path, so we assume no bone pieces are left on top.

phrases.english: is pure for those bringing the Pesach offering.
They did not uphold their words in a place of karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 11, different from שמואל's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Checking means seeing whether the בית הפרס has been trodden down. If it has, it is pure for the פסח, because a rule of the רבנן does not stand where כרת is at stake.

steps.title: For eating תרומה the rule stayed in force
steps.stepSummary: עולא continues: for people who want to eat תרומה, the רבנן kept their בית הפרס rule even where a death penalty is at stake.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for people eating תרומה, the רבנן kept their words in force, even where the punishment is death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes עולא's statement from the last step. He now gives the other side: for תרומה, the strict rule stays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who skips the פסח gets כרת, so the רבנן relaxed their rule there. Eating תרומה while impure is punished by death from Heaven, and yet the רבנן kept their rule in place for תרומה. So the leniency is only for the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן. It may only be eaten in purity.
They kept their words in force; their rule still applies
Death, meaning death at the hands of Heaven

phrases.english: For those eating terumah
they upheld their words
in a place of death.
phrases.notes: A כהן who eats תרומה while impure is punished with death from Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאוֹכְלֵי תְרוּמָה הֶעֱמִידוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶן בִּמְקוֹם מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes עולא's statement that began in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית הפרס rule stays in force for eating תרומה, even though a death penalty is involved.

steps.title: Does a check made for the פסח also allow תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask: if someone checked the בית הפרס so he could bring his פסח, may he also eat his תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if a person checked the field for his פסח, may he eat his תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question that grows out of עולא's rule. It is setting up a disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know the check works for the פסח but is not enough for תרומה on its own. The question is about a person who already checked for the פסח and was found pure. Does that pure status carry over to his תרומה too?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
He checked (the ground of the בית הפרס)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If he checked for his paschal offering,
phrases.notes: This is the check for the בית הפרס discussed in steps 12 and 13.

phrases.english: what is the law, may he eat his terumah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the split between פסח and תרומה in steps 13 and 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a check done for the פסח also make the person pure for תרומה?

steps.title: עולא: He may eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that once a person checked for his פסח, he may also eat his תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: if he checked for his פסח, he is allowed to eat his תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question and is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once this person has been treated as pure for the פסח, it would not make sense to call him impure for תרומה at the same moment. His pure status counts for both.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
If he checked for his paschal offering,
he is permitted to eat his terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A check done for the פסח also allows him to eat תרומה.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: He may not eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא disagrees and rules that he may not eat his תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: if he checked for his פסח, he is forbidden to eat his תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא answers the same question the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה בר עולא, the check only works where the רבנן relaxed their rule, which is the פסח. For תרומה the rule was kept in force, so the check does not help there.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two names: עולא is lenient, and רבה בר עולא is strict.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
If he checked for his paschal offering,
he is forbidden to eat his terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with עולא's answer in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The check helps only for the פסח, not for תרומה.

steps.title: An old man supports עולא from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: An old man tells רבה בר עולא not to argue with עולא. Our משנה believes an עם הארץ about the קודש in a barrel, and so he is also believed about the תרומה in it. The same should be true for פסח and תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain old man said to him: Don't argue with עולא, because our משנה matches his view. It says that if the עם הארץ says 'I put a רביעית of קודש into this barrel,' he is believed. So once he is believed about קודש, he is believed about the תרומה too. Here as well, once he is believed about the פסח, he is believed about תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: An old man brings a proof for עולא from the line of our משנה quoted in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the barrel holds תרומה with a little קודש mixed in. Because the עם הארץ is trusted about the קודש, the whole barrel, תרומה included, is treated as pure. The old man applies the same idea here: being pure for the פסח carries over to תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain old man (an unnamed elder)
A quarter-לוג, a small measure of liquid
So we see, this shows that

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets out a principle: when one area is treated as pure, a closely linked area is treated as pure too. The flasks discussion right after uses the same kind of reasoning.

phrases.english: A certain old man said to him:
phrases.notes: He is talking to רבה בר עולא.

phrases.english: Do not argue with Ulla,
for we learned in a mishna in accordance with him:
And if he said: I set aside into it
phrases.notes: This is the line of our משנה quoted in step 9. 'It' is the barrel of תרומה.

phrases.english: a quarter-log of sacred wine or oil, he is believed.
So we see: since he is believed about the sacred,
he is believed about the terumah too.
Here too: since he is believed regarding the paschal offering,
he is believed regarding terumah too.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּפְלוֹג עֲלֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא, דִּתְנַן כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports עולא in the disagreement of steps 16 and 17.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's ruling that a check for the פסח also allows eating תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: an עם הארץ is believed when he says he put a רביעית of קודש into a barrel of תרומה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Being trusted for the stricter area (קודש or פסח) carries over to תרומה, so our משנה supports עולא's view.

steps.title: A ברייתא: Not believed about flasks or תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the line of our משנה about jugs of wine and oil. It quotes a ברייתא: an עם הארץ is not believed about flasks or about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה said: 'Jugs of wine and jugs of oil, etc.' A ברייתא taught: they are not believed about the flasks, and not about the תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of our משנה and brings a ברייתא on it. This sets up a question about what the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה believes an עם הארץ about mixed (מדומעות) jugs of wine and oil during the pressing season. The ברייתא adds limits: in some cases he is not believed about the flasks, and not about the תרומה.

phrases.english: Jugs of wine and jugs of oil, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the rest of that line in our משנה, which is about being believed during the pressing season.

phrases.english: A Sage taught: They are not believed

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל הַקַּנְקַנִּים וְלֹא עַל הַתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: neither about the flasks nor about the terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עם הארץ is not believed about flasks or about תרומה.

steps.title: Which flasks does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of flasks the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Flasks of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. It is setting up two possible answers that it will test next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flasks could hold קודש or they could hold תרומה. The meaning of the ברייתא depends on which one.

phrases.english: Flasks of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא in step 19 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are these flasks of קודש or flasks of תרומה?

steps.title: Not flasks of קודש, since he is believed on the קודש
steps.stepSummary: Flasks of קודש cannot be meant, because if he is believed about the קודש itself, he should also be believed about its flasks.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say flasks of קודש: since he is believed about the קודש, he should also be believed about the flasks!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and shows it cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is trusted about קודש all year round. It would make no sense to trust him about the contents but not about the container that holds them. This uses a מיגו argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because he is trusted on one thing, he is trusted on the related thing
Sacred items, here wine or oil for the מקדש

phrases.english: If it means flasks of sacred items,
since he is believed about the sacred items,
he should be believed about the flasks too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַנְקַנִּים דְּקֹדֶשׁ — מִיגּוֹ דִּמְהֵימַן אַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as flasks of קודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trust about the contents must extend to the container, so the ברייתא could not say he is not believed about flasks of קודש.

steps.title: Flasks of תרומה would be too obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא means flasks of תרומה, that is obvious. If he is not even believed about the תרומה, of course he is not believed about its flasks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, flasks of תרומה? That is obvious! If he is not believed about the תרומה itself, would he be believed about the flasks?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option and finds that the ברייתא would then be saying something too obvious to need saying. Step 23 gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is not trusted about תרומה. So saying he is not trusted about flasks of תרומה adds nothing new. Both options now seem to fail, and the גמרא must find another explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why would this need to be taught?

phrases.english: Rather, it means flasks of terumah,
that is obvious!
Now, if he is not believed about the terumah,
would he be believed about the flasks?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible answer after the first one failed in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as flasks of תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he is not trusted about the תרומה itself, of course he is not trusted about its flasks, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The ברייתא means empty קודש flasks, and full תרומה flasks at winepress time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's 'not believed about flasks' refers to empty flasks of קודש during the rest of the year, and to full flasks of תרומה during winepress time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא is talking about empty flasks of קודש during the rest of the year, and about full flasks of תרומה during the time of the winepresses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question about which flasks the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All year long an עם הארץ is believed about קודש itself, but once a flask of קודש is empty, he is not believed about the flask. At winepress time he is believed about the תרומה itself, but not about the flasks that hold it. So in both cases the ברייתא is teaching something new about the flasks.

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the days of the year
Winepress time, when an עם הארץ is believed about תרומה

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer gets the ברייתא past both problems from Steps 21 and 22: it no longer clashes with the rule for קודש, and it is no longer obvious.

phrases.english: Rather, it is talking about empty flasks of קודש
phrases.notes: These are flasks that used to hold קודש and have now been emptied.

phrases.english: and during the rest of the days of the year,
and about full flasks of תרומה
during the time of the winepresses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from Steps 21 and 22 by giving the ברייתא a new case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to mean flasks of קודש or flasks of תרומה in the ordinary sense, and both readings failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means empty קודש flasks all year, and full תרומה flasks at winepress time.

steps.title: Our משנה believes him about jugs mixed with תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה believes an עם הארץ about jugs of wine and oil that are מדומעות. That sounds like jugs mixed with תרומה, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in our משנה: jugs of wine and jugs of oil that are מדומעות. Doesn't that mean they are mixed with תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave, using the words of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מדומע usually means a mixture with תרומה. Our משנה believes the עם הארץ about these jugs. But the ברייתא, as just explained, says he is not believed about flasks of תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed, usually ordinary food mixed with תרומה
What, isn't it so that...? (opening a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן הַמְדוּמָּעוֹת.
phrases.english: We learned: jugs of wine and jugs of oil that are mixed.
What, does it not mean mixed with תרומה?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן הַמְדוּמָּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 23 from our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an עם הארץ is not believed about flasks of תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מדומעות means mixed with תרומה, our משנה believes him about תרומה jugs, which goes against the ברייתא.

steps.title: The school of רבי חייא: the jugs are mixed with קודש
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי חייא explains that our משנה means jugs mixed with קודש, not with תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי חייא said: it means mixed with קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה's jugs as holding a mixture of קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is believed about קודש, so he is also believed about its jugs. Nothing here goes against the ברייתא's rule for תרומה flasks.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי חייא says

phrases.english: In the school of רבי חייא they say:
mixed with קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzMaskana: מדומעות here means mixed with קודש.

steps.title: Is the word דימוע ever used for קודש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the word דימוע is ever used for קודש at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there such a thing as דימוע for קודש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי חייא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The term דימוע belongs to תרומה. Calling a mixture of קודש 'מדומע' sounds like the wrong word, so the answer seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture, the term used for תרומה mixed into ordinary food

phrases.english: And is there such a thing as a mixture for קודש?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's reading that the משנה's jugs are mixed with קודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word מדומע is used only for תרומה, so it does not fit a mixture of קודש.

steps.title: The school of רבי אלעאי: טבל kept pure for נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי אלעאי explains the case: a person keeps his טבל wine pure so that he can take נסכים from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אלעאי said: the case is someone who keeps his טבל pure so that he can take נסכים from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a case where the word מדומע fits and קודש is still involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This טבל wine has תרומה inside it that has not been separated yet, so it really is מדומע. Part of it is also meant for נסכים, which is קודש. Since the עם הארץ is believed about the קודש part, he is believed about the whole jug.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been separated
Wine libations poured on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the explanation of רבי חייא, so both our משנה and the ברייתא can stand.

phrases.english: In the school of רבי אלעאי they say:
it is about one who keeps his טבל pure
in order to take libations from it.
phrases.notes: So the jug holds a future קודש part and unseparated תרומה together. That is why it can be called מדומע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 26 and supports Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a specific case where both words fit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מדומע cannot describe something that involves קודש.
steps.terutzMaskana: טבל kept pure for נסכים is both מדומע, because of its תרומה, and also connected to קודש.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא: he is not believed about empty קודש flasks, or about תרומה flasks at winepress time. Our משנה: he is believed about jugs of טבל kept pure for נסכים, because of the קודש in them.

steps.title: אביי: a tenant farmer must prepare flasks seventy days before the winepress
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'seventy days before the winepresses,' אביי learns that a tenant farmer must start working on the flasks seventy days before the pressing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: seventy days before the winepresses. אביי said: learn from this that it is the law that a tenant farmer must take the trouble to prepare the flasks seventy days before the winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה, and אביי draws a practical business law from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the seventy days before pressing as part of the winepress season, because that is when people get ready. אביי learns from this that preparing the flasks during that time is part of a tenant farmer's job.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenant farmer who works a field for a share of its crop
To take the trouble, to work at

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a purity rule in a משנה can teach a practical law about work agreements.

phrases.english: Seventy days before the winepresses.
אביי said: learn from this:
it is the law that it is upon the tenant farmer
to take the trouble over the flasks
seventy days before the winepress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה, the seventy days before the winepress.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tenant farmer must prepare the wine flasks starting seventy days before the winepress.

steps.title: Potters inside מודיעים are believed about clay pots
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה sets a boundary. Inside מודיעים, potters are believed about the טהרה of earthenware vessels. Outside it, they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: From מודיעים inward, potters are believed about clay vessels. From מודיעים outward, they are not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It draws a line at the town of מודיעים: potters inside the line are believed about their clay pots, and potters outside it are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an עם הארץ is not trusted about טהרה. This משנה makes a special exception for earthenware vessels in the area around ירושלים, up to מודיעים. The exception has a clear geographic limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the main text being studied
A town some distance from ירושלים that marks the boundary
They are believed (trusted to say the item is טהור)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole discussion that follows. Trust about clay pots depends on location, measured from מודיעים.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
From Modi'im and inward,
phrases.notes: 'Inward' means on the ירושלים side of מודיעים.

phrases.english: they are believed about earthenware vessels.
From Modi'im and outward —
they are not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן הַמּוֹדִיעִים וְלִפְנִים נֶאֱמָנִין עַל כְּלֵי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after אביי's teaching about the seventy days before the winepresses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inside מודיעים, potters are believed about the טהרה of earthenware. Outside it, they are not.

steps.title: It depends on where the potter is right now
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives an example. The same potter, with the same pots and the same buyers, is believed once he enters the boundary and is not believed once he leaves it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A potter who sells pots entered inside מודיעים. Even though it is the same potter, the same pots and the same buyers, he is believed. If he went out, he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its rule with a case. A potter's trust switches on or off depending on which side of מודיעים he is standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a potter who came from outside is still untrusted, because nothing about him or his pots changed. The משנה says no: only his present location counts. The reverse is also true. If he leaves, he loses that trust.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the pots carry a fixed status from where they were made. The משנה stresses that the very same potter, pots and buyers become trusted or untrusted just by crossing the line.

phrases.english: How so?
The potter who sells the pots,
if he entered inside Modi'im,
though it is the same potter and the same pots
and the same buyers — he is believed;
phrases.notes: Meaning these were all outside a moment ago, where he would not have been believed.

phrases.english: if he went out — he is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the boundary rule of step 29 with a concrete case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The potter's present location decides whether he is believed, even when the same potter, pots and buyers were outside before.

steps.title: A ברייתא: מודיעים itself can count as inside or outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. The town of מודיעים itself is sometimes treated as inside the boundary and sometimes as outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא: מודיעים itself is sometimes like inside and sometimes like outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא about the boundary town itself. This line sets up the examples that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'from מודיעים inward' and 'from מודיעים outward', but it did not say how to treat מודיעים itself. The ברייתא answers that it has a double status. It does not fall wholly on one side.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was taught: Modi'im itself —
sometimes it is like inside,
sometimes it is like outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מוֹדִיעִים פְּעָמִים כְּלִפְנִים פְּעָמִים כְּלַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills a gap in the משנה's boundary by stating how to treat the boundary town itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מודיעים has a double status. Sometimes it counts as inside and sometimes as outside.

steps.title: When מודיעים counts as inside
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives its first case. If the potter is leaving and the חבר is entering, מודיעים counts as inside. It then begins a second case where both are entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If a potter is going out and a חבר is coming in, and they meet there, it is like inside. If both are coming in...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains when מודיעים counts as inside: the potter is heading out and the חבר is heading in. It then starts the next case, both of them entering, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the חבר may treat the meeting as if it happened inside and rely on the potter. The second case, where both are coming in, is about to show the opposite side of the double status. That case is still in progress.

keyTerms.meaning: A person careful about טהרה laws

phrases.english: How so?
If a potter is going out and a ḥaver is coming in —
phrases.notes: They meet each other in מודיעים itself.

phrases.english: it is like inside.
If both are coming in…

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the concrete examples of the double status announced in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the potter is leaving and the חבר is entering, מודיעים counts as inside. The case of both entering begins here and continues.
